_comment: 🧩️ XLSX ECMA-376/🧱️base's own contribution to the repository test platform — its mutation oracle registration and its declared mutation vocabulary (wave 7, ticket 26/08/23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR). Discovered by convention alongside ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own top-level manifest; merged into one registry, no central edit required. Registers ONE oracle id for the reference PAIRING this subset needs (no single crate both reads and modifies an XLSX): `calamine` 0.36 parses a real workbook into resolved cell data; `rust_xlsxwriter` 0.96 assembles a brand-new package from a grid built out of that read — never opens and patches the original. Worksheet and cell mutations are independently readable as a per-sheet grid; `insert-cell` additionally carries a revision-guarded vacancy address and has a native Calamine save/read law. The three shared-string mutations address the shared-string pool by an INDEX independent of any cell reference — the one axis neither crate exposes (`calamine`'s own `strings: Vec<String>` field and `read_shared_strings` method are both private; `rust_xlsxwriter`'s shared-string table is populated only as a byproduct of `write_string` on a cell, with no API to target an entry directly) — so their `mutate`/`inverse` scenarios are `@mode-round-trip`/`@mode-property` instead of `@mode-differential`; see the Feature file's own description and this subset's `🦀️.rs` module doc comment for the full reasoning.

oracles.rationale:
🩹️ RECLASSIFIED (ticket SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION, shard A10, 2026-09-02). This entry was registered `third-party-library` on the strength of a real crate that does genuine codec work, but the mutation's expected RESULT is computed by this owner's own `🦀️.rs` -- its dispatch function's catch-all arm is `"mutation kind {...} has no oracle implementation"`, proof that every OTHER arm is an implementation, not a reading. Both halves of the comparison then descend from the same specification, so a shared misreading produces two agreeing wrong answers -- the one failure a differential oracle exists to catch. This is a `cross-semio-implementation`: a required SUPPLEMENT (metamorphic/inverse/round-trip evidence), never a substitute. A qualifying third-party reference for the mutation semantics is still owed. See $TICKET/📓️a10-oracle-honesty.md.

The reference ECMA-376 SpreadsheetML reader of the Rust ecosystem, paired with the reference writer `rust_xlsxwriter` 0.96 (MIT OR Apache-2.0, https://github.com/jmcnamara/rust_xlsxwriter), declared as this entry's linked `packages` member so the dependency ratchet and the oracle-purity probe classify it in its own right rather than only reading about it here for the seven mutation kinds this pairing can independently reproduce end to end (read the real workbook into a per-sheet cell grid, apply the change to the grid, rebuild the whole workbook from it — the only channel available, since `rust_xlsxwriter` cannot open and patch an existing package). Registered under `calamine` because every scenario's comparison runs through `calamine` as the independent reader on BOTH sides (oracle output and subject output alike), matching how this catalog's `@oracle-` tag names a single id per feature. `rust_xlsxwriter` is the paired producer for the differential kinds and is exercised by every green `@mode-differential` scenario even though it is not the package name on this entry; it is registered under this entry's `packages` list, which is what puts it inside the same test-only ratchet as `calamine`.

packages.role: independent SpreadsheetML writer — the producing half `calamine` does not have

oracles.rationale: 📖️ A READER, registered separately from this file's existing `cross-semio-implementation` entry, which COMPUTES what a mutation should produce from this repository's own reading of the spec and therefore cannot discharge this requirement — both halves would descend from one reading of it. openpyxl 3.1.5 is a from-scratch reader/writer of the SpreadsheetML package (its own OPC walk, its own XML parsing — no dependency on this repository's `zip`/`calamine`/`quick-xml` reimplementation). `load_workbook(path)` exposes `wb.sheetnames`, `ws.dimensions`, per-cell `ws[coord].value`, and cell formatting/formula strings, directly witnessing this subset's document vocabulary. Verified against this subset's own committed `shared://📕️reuse-marketplaces.xlsx`: `wb.sheetnames` reports the real two-sheet workbook (`Marktplätze`, `Länderübersicht`) and `ws['A1'].value` reads the real header cell `ID`.

📖️ A third-party implementation of the OPC package layer: jszip opens the container and fast-xml-parser reads and writes `[Content_Types].xml` and every `*.rels` part. The `before`/`after` pairs of the plumbing kinds are authored from the artifact's committed real package by this pairing -- each pair states its effect once as an XML edit and once as a model-level expectation and is refused unless both agree -- so nothing in this repository predicts the answer the pairs are judged against.

comparisonProfiles.description: XLSX workbooks compared by their real per-sheet cell grid (sheet name, then every non-empty cell's row/col/resolved value, read independently by `calamine` on both sides) PLUS a caller-tracked `sharedStringCount` field — `calamine` exposes no accessor for the raw shared-string pool size (see this subset's `🦀️.rs` module doc comment), so that one field is supplied by the case adapter rather than derived from the projected bytes: the oracle side by structural arithmetic on the applied kind, the subject side by reading its own real `XlsxWorkbook::shared_strings.len()`. `Number` cells carry a small floating-point tolerance since ECMA-376 stores every number as an IEEE-754 double and two independent writers may round the same value's textual form a few ULPs apart.
